content: The development of effective self-management skills is essential during the transition period when adolescents move from family-centered diabetes management to independently managing their condition. This process requires the acquisition of comprehensive knowledge about diabetes, including understanding blood glucose monitoring, insulin administration, carbohydrate counting, and recognizing symptoms of hypoor hyperglycemia. Additionally, it involves mastering the ability to make informed decisions regarding lifestyle choices, such as diet, physical activity, and adherence to prescribed treatment regimens. The transition also demands the capacity to navigate healthcare systems, schedule medical appointments, and communicate effectively with healthcare providers.
